Let  
\[
S=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{\cos n\theta}{2^n}.
\]
This is the real part of the complex geometric series
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(\frac{e^{i\theta}}{2}\right)^n
=\frac{1}{1-\frac{e^{i\theta}}{2}}.
\]
Thus,
\[
S=\Re\left(\frac{1}{1-\frac{e^{i\theta}}{2}}\right).
\]
Simplify:
\[
\frac{1}{1-\frac{e^{i\theta}}{2}}
=\frac{2}{2-e^{i\theta}}.
\]
The real part is
\[
S=\frac{1-\frac12\cos\theta}{1-\cos\theta+\frac14}
\]
or equivalently
\[
S=\frac{1-r\cos\theta}{1-2r\cos\theta+r^2},\qquad r=\frac12.
\]
Given \(\cos\theta=\frac15\), we get
\[
S=\frac{1-\frac12\cdot\frac15}{1-2\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac15+\left(\frac12\right)^2}
=\frac{1-\frac1{10}}{1-\frac15+\frac14}.
\]
Compute:
\[
S=\frac{\frac{9}{10}}{\frac{21}{20}}
=\frac{9}{10}\cdot\frac{20}{21}
=\frac{18}{21}
=\frac67.
\]

The answer is \(\frac67\).
